Walking through Anping Old Street feels like stepping back in time, with its narrow lanes, historic charm, and lively atmosphere. The street is packed with food stalls offering a variety of Taiwanese snacks, from crispy shrimp rolls to freshly grilled squid.
One of my favorite finds was the coffin bread, a thick toast filled with creamy seafood or chicken—it’s both delicious and fun to eat!
During my visit to Anping, I had the chance to try a traditional Chinese massage with oil, and it was exactly what I needed. After walking around all day, my body was aching, and I was feeling a bit under the weather. The massage therapist used a combination of deep pressure and smooth oil techniques to relieve tension and improve circulation.

What stood out the most was how they incorporated traditional Chinese medicine principles. The therapist focused on specific pressure points and energy pathways, helping to ease body aches and restore balance. The herbal-infused oil added to the experience, providing a warm, soothing sensation that left me feeling refreshed and rejuvenated.

If you’re ever in Anping and need relief from travel fatigue or body aches, I highly recommend trying a Chinese oil massage. It’s not just relaxing—it’s a true healing experience!

Shennong Street (神农街), located in Tainan, Taiwan, is a vibrant hub of artistic expression. Once steeped in history, it has transformed into a dynamic space where old buildings now house trendy cafés, artist studios, designer boutiques, and modern guesthouses.

The atmosphere strikes a delicate balance between tradition and innovation: while the walls still echo stories of the past, the creative energy pulsing through every corner feels decidedly forward-looking. The street enchants with its curated aesthetic and cosmopolitan vibe, drawing both art enthusiasts and casual wanderers in search of inspiration.

Achieving this harmony between memory and renewal is no small feat, but Shennong Street pulls it off with remarkable finesse.

Visiting Anping Fort in Tainan is like stepping back into the pages of history, where the echoes of past empires linger in the air. The fort, originally built by the Dutch in the 17th century, serves as a reminder of Taiwan’s complex colonial past and its resilient spirit.

The approach to the fort is marked by a striking staircase of weathered red bricks, leading up to the main entrance. The architecture blends European military design with local materials, creating a uniquely Taiwanese landmark. The bare branches of ancient trees frame the fort, their silhouettes adding to the timeless atmosphere.

One of the highlights is the statue of Koxinga, the Ming Dynasty general who seized the fort from the Dutch. Standing proud against the backdrop of the old walls, it’s a testament to his enduring legacy in Taiwan. Exploring the fort with family was a special experience—seeing my mother and loved ones beside such historic monuments added a personal touch to the visit.

The restored buildings within the fort showcase traditional Chinese architecture, complete with blue-tiled roofs and elegant arches. It’s a serene spot to reflect on the cultural blend that defines modern Taiwan. My mother, standing beside the monument engraved with the characters “安平古堡” (Anping Fort), was a poignant moment—bridging generations amidst a backdrop of endurance and peace.

If you find yourself in Tainan, Anping Fort is a must-visit. It’s not just about the history, but also about the layers of stories that come alive through its walls and pathways. It’s a place that invites you to ponder the past while enjoying the present—an experience both profound and humbling.

Yuguang Island, situated in the East China Sea, captivates visitors with its natural beauty and cultural allure. The island's pristine beaches, adorned with golden sands and crystal-clear waters, create a serene atmosphere for relaxation. Nature enthusiasts can explore lush green landscapes, featuring diverse flora and fauna that add to the island's ecological charm.

Culturally, Yuguang Island is a treasure trove. Its historical sites, including ancient temples and traditional fishing villages, provide a glimpse into the region's rich heritage. The islanders' warm hospitality and dedication to preserving their traditions contribute to a truly immersive experience.

For adventure seekers, Yuguang offers exciting water activities such as snorkeling and sailing, taking advantage of its coastal location. Local seafood delicacies are a culinary highlight, showcasing the freshest catches from the surrounding waters.

While the island provides a perfect escape for those seeking tranquility, its blend of natural wonders and cultural heritage offers a well-rounded experience for any traveler. Yuguang Island emerges as a hidden gem, inviting exploration and leaving visitors with lasting memories of a delightful getaway.

(2021.1.31) The current situation of the fort historic site is quite delicate(?). Due to the lease of public land, the fort was leased to Shuzenyuan after World War II until now. What I want to say in particular is that when I was walking up the stairs to savor the taste, I bumped my head against the building next to me without paying attention... It can be seen that there are traces of the temple's manipulations on the exterior of the fort building. So what can be done now is to maintain the status quo and maintain it as much as possible. The stay was not long, we visited quickly and left quickly.

2023.1.6

reviews.text: A really interesting history. It was very quiet when I visited.

History Yongkang Sugar Factory was formerly known as Xingfa Sugar Factory. It was operated by British Harry Hastings in 1904 (Meiji 37th year). In 1906 (Meiji 39th year), it was affiliated to the British merchant Yiji Foreign Company and renamed Sankandian Sugar Factory. In 1912 (Taisho 1st Year), it was merged by Taiwan Sugar Co., Ltd. and renamed Sankandian Factory, with a crushing capacity of 850 tons. After the Taiwan Sugar Company was established in 1945 (the 34th year of the Republic of China), it went through several name changes and mergers, and stopped sugar production in 1990 (the 79th year of the Republic of China). In the factory area, there is a Sankandian shrine established during the Japanese colonial period, which is dedicated to Prince Noku, Amaterasu and Toyoshou. After World War II, the Taiwanese built a post office on the shrine, which became a post office in the neighboring area at that time. My own experience of this place was wonderful this is because saw the remnant of Taiwan City Wall and the history of it.
This is the only remnant of the original Taiwan city wall. It is still standing there.
There is a beautiful little flower garden in front. The red bricks are very distinctive and beautiful.

It was originally the city wall of Relanja City. It was made by mixing sugar water, glutinous rice juice, oyster shells, and sand, and then stacking bricks. The Dutch were called red-haired fans by their ancestors. They said that this technology used "red-haired soil", which is stronger and more durable than the traditional rammed earth construction method.
Now only a broken wall remains for tourists to recall the prosperity of that year.

I hope this letter finds you in good health and high spirits. Though I am writing from a different time, your courage and selfless dedication to justice continue to inspire generations of people who believe in democracy, human rights, and the rule of law.

If you were here today, I would want to tell you that your ideals have not been in vain. Though the road to justice has been long and difficult, Taiwan has grown into a free and democratic society—one where your dreams of fairness and human rights are cherished and upheld. We remember you not as a victim of history but as a hero who paved the way for a brighter future.

Thank you for your courage. Thank you for your sacrifice. And thank you for showing us the power of standing up for what is right.

With deepest respect,
Michael Liu

you are a very brave fighter what you do to the community is very commendable. Your dedication to defending the rights of the people, even in the face of grave danger, is an inspiration to generations.Thank you for your bravery. Thank you for your unwavering belief in justice. The world remembers you, and we honor your memory by continuing the fight for human rights and freedom.

Tang Dezhang Memorial Park is a powerful tribute to a man who stood for justice and the rights of the oppressed during a turbulent period in Taiwan's history. The park serves not only as a place of remembrance but also as a reminder of the sacrifices made for the greater good. The peaceful environment offers visitors a chance to reflect on the injustices of the past and honor the courage of those like Tang Dezhang, who fought for a better future. It's a meaningful place where history meets remembrance.

This event had a big impact on Taiwan , including human right violations and the actions of those in power. Because of this, more people understood the bad effects of unfair control. You spoke up for the people but faced unfair punishment. But to me, you were very brave for standing up for everyone.

Tang Te-chang was a Taiwanese lawyer who fought for justice. He helped victims and kept order in Tainan, but the government said he was a rebel. On March 13, 1947, he was executed in Tainan Park. Before he died, he asked people to remember justice. Later, the park was renamed “Tang Te-chang Memorial Park” to honor him.

reviews.text:
Taijiang National Park, managed by the National Park Service under the Ministry of the Interior, is a captivating natural and cultural treasure in Taiwan. The park seamlessly blends diverse ecosystems, historical sites, and traditional communities, creating a rich tapestry of experiences.

The park's headquarters serve as a gateway to this splendid landscape, providing visitors with valuable information and resources. The staff's commitment to environmental education and conservation is commendable, fostering a sense of stewardship among visitors.

One of the park's highlights is its unique biodiversity, encompassing coastal wetlands, mangrove forests, and vibrant marine life. Nature enthusiasts will appreciate the well-maintained trails and observation points that showcase the park's ecological wonders.

Moreover, Taijiang National Park preserves Taiwan's cultural heritage with historic sites and traditional villages, allowing visitors to delve into the island's past. The integration of local communities into the park's management enhances the authenticity of the experience.

In summary, Taijiang National Park is a testament to Taiwan's dedication to preserving its natural and cultural legacy. The harmonious coexistence of nature and human history makes it a must-visit destination for those seeking a profound connection with Taiwan's essence.

Daan Forest Park (大安森林公園) offers a serene escape in the heart of Taipei, and its ecological pond is truly the gem of the park. Surrounded by lush greenery, this area is a haven for wildlife and a perfect spot for nature lovers and families alike.

The pond is teeming with life—colorful fish dart through the water, turtles bask lazily on rocks, and various bird species can be seen gliding gracefully or perched on nearby branches. During my visit, I was thrilled to spot a few kingfishers and egrets, which added a magical touch to the experience.

What makes the ecological pond special is its emphasis on preserving a natural environment. The landscape feels intentionally wild yet thoughtfully maintained, creating a peaceful space that encourages quiet observation and reflection. Informational signs around the area help you learn more about the flora and fauna, making it both educational and enjoyable.

A Thread of Sky (一線天) is a striking natural feature located along the Xiangshan Trail, offering a unique and picturesque stop for hikers. This narrow rock formation creates a dramatic “slice” of sky between towering cliffs, making it a fascinating and photogenic spot that feels almost otherworldly.

Reaching A Thread of Sky involves a bit of climbing, but the trail leading there is manageable and well-marked. As you approach, the light filtering through the rocky crevice creates a stunning effect, especially during early morning or late afternoon. It’s a great place to pause, take in the beauty of nature, and capture some memorable photos.

The Liberty Square Arch (自由廣場牌樓) is a breathtaking architectural marvel and a proud symbol of Taiwan’s cultural and democratic identity. Serving as the grand entrance to Liberty Square, this magnificent archway is one of Taipei’s most photographed landmarks—and for good reason.

Standing tall at 30 meters, the arch features five beautifully proportioned gates, with the central one symbolizing openness and freedom. The intricate carvings, traditional Chinese motifs, and vibrant blue tile roof showcase exceptional craftsmanship and attention to detail. The inscription “自由廣場” (Freedom Square) boldly proclaims the nation’s commitment to liberty and democracy, making it a powerful sight for visitors and locals alike.

This is a must do for people that like a moderate challenge and want a great view of the city. There are about 600 steps to get to the top, but if it’s too much of a challenge there is a viewpoint a little more than halfway. But don’t give up. Take your time and get to the top viewpoint. It’s much better and you can see so much more of the city. We went at night to see the city lit up. The stairs are lit for almost the entire path and there are hand rails for the steepest parts. Despite its name of Elephant Mountain, you won’t see one elephant ☹️ but you will have a great view.

A lot of stairs! Hahah 😂 much like Koreas hikes. Definitely worth the view during the night though with all the lights of the city area. Right after you get off of Tamsui station, it’s straight for the park location, you will pass by the basketball courts on your left side and then take a left at the end of the street go up the road to the very end, then take a right and then about 25 m there is a steep staircase. That is the entry point for the hike 😂🫡

reviews.text: A great spot for photo-taking, though unfortunately, it was drizzling during my visit. The fog obscured most of Taipei 101, making it barely visible. Nonetheless, it is still an excellent hiking trail and perfect for a good workout!

A beautiful hiking trail in the heart of the city, perfect place to see (or take pictures) of 101, easily accessible (trail entrance is 7 min walk from XiangShan MRT Exit 2).  Many steps, some small, some larger.  Lots of sitting areas along the path for hikers to rest.  The giant boulders are along the trail path (~10 min from trail entrance).  Keep going another few minutes for an amazing vantage point of 101 skyscraper and the city.  Many trail option (see map).  You can decide how high and how far to hike!  Do remember to bring water.
This is a famous place to watch Taipei 101. You can hike up to the hill and enjoy the trail.

Taipei is a city with an endless amount of things to see and do - but its fair to say that the undisputed champion of the city’s tourist attractions is the Elephant Mountain Hiking Trail. This is why each and every day hundreds, if not thousands of photos are posted from the many popular photo spots on the trail.You’re of course welcome to disagree with my assessment, but before you do, I recommend taking some time to hike the mountain and taking note of the amazing mixture of languages being spoken by all of the travelers on the trail. You’re not likely to have an even remotely similar experience anywhere else in Taiwan (at least not in such a high concentration) as you will on Elephant Mountain.

reviews.text: There are cherry blossom trees in front of Citi Bank building. It is also a good spot in capturing Taipei 101.

When I first came here, I felt very comfortable with the open design and clean environment of the square. The square is surrounded by green trees and has seating and shade areas in the center, perfect for stopping and enjoying some quiet time. I found many people chatting here with coffee, and there were also citizens running or practicing yoga. The overall atmosphere was very peaceful and natural.

The biggest highlight here is the markets or cultural activities held from time to time. I was lucky enough to come across a handmade market, and the stalls displayed a variety of specialty products, from handmade soaps to illustrations, each of which was full of creativity. There were also live music performances, filling the entire square with a vibrant and pleasant atmosphere.

Although the Taipei City Government East Gate Plaza is not large, it provides a space where you can slow down and integrate with the city and nature. Whether you are just passing by or visiting on purpose, it is worth spending some time here to enjoy the little blessings in life!

It has been raining in Taipei for more than ten consecutive days, and I feel very depressed.
It’s like this year’s epidemic has caused such complete chaos...

In order to welcome the new year 2021,
The installation art "Smile Ark" in front of the East Gate Square of the Municipal Government,
There are sound and light effects and interactions, which is quite interesting.
Although in the rain...the colorful colors look more artistic~

The city government claims to ensure that Instagram will never run out of beautiful photos~
However, the style looks too much like the international superstar Mi XX!
I wonder if this artist is worried...

There are also various lighting decorations around the city hall.
Like a sidewalk embraced by big hands,
Shining silver canopy lighting, etc.,
However, the lighting design is not strong enough.
The small lights around the tree trunk are too sparse!

Let’s talk about it again
The fonts used in promotional materials are old and traditional, and they are barely used in school assignments.
It’s really not suitable for use at such a large urban event~
If you can use calligraphy poster fonts to design promotional materials,
It can relatively improve the high-quality urban quality of Taipei.

reviews.text: Came here to see the flowers including cherry blossoms. There are lots of flowers but the cherry blossoms were seen on the way up. So we missed the opportunity to see them. Nice place to hike and take in greenery and fresh air. Went on a public holiday hence was pretty crowded. Some scenic spots to catch cherry blossoms too.

A beautiful park and it was a very well taken care of and the staff were so kind at the visitor center. It was a beautiful day when I went, but cloudy and that stunk, considering I wanted to do the Mt. Qixing peak.

I still did the loop and the peak, because it was so beautiful on the way up and totally worth the workout! Bring your waters, electrolytes, and snacks! Bring a jacket too if you go in the winter! You might hit rain or a wind chill the higher you climb!

Also, story time! The National Forest Guards are so helpful! I left my apple watch on a portable charger up on the mountain trail head and the park had just closed and the buses going up had stopped. I talked to some locals that drove me down the mountain to the ranger station and they drove me all the way back up to grab my watch, which was still there! They were so incredibly kind and funny about the whole situation!

Another international park knocked off the list, and it was lovely! I hope to come back during the summer and enjoy the clear skies!

The main reason I came up here was to visit the Flower Clock. Upon taking a bus from Taipei Main Station, I reached the Yangmingshan bus terminal in like 40-ish minutes. Upon ascending the mountain, I was greeted with thick mist on the way to the bus terminal and this is in March.

At the bus terminal, I still had to take another bus to the Flower Clock.

Really beautiful national park, you can visit the mountains and smell the sulfur. There’s also an area to soak your feet in the hot springs and walk around the area. The view is incredibly beautiful and the nature is so incredible

Ximending Walking District is one of the most vibrant and bustling areas in Taipei, and it’s a must-visit for both locals and tourists! The district is packed with shops, restaurants, cafes, street food vendors, and entertainment, making it the perfect place to explore. You can find everything from trendy fashion boutiques to quirky stores selling unique Taiwanese souvenirs.

The area has a youthful, energetic vibe, with performers and street artists adding to the lively atmosphere. It’s also great for food lovers—there are plenty of delicious snacks, such as bubble tea, Taiwanese fried chicken, and traditional desserts.

Whether you’re shopping, dining, or just enjoying the street performances, Ximending Walking District has something for everyone. Highly recommended for anyone looking to experience the heart of Taipei’s entertainment and culture!

Taipei North Gate is an awe-inspiring historic landmark that truly embodies the rich cultural heritage of Taipei, Taiwan. Built during the Qing Dynasty in the 19th century, the gate served as an integral part of the city's defensive fortifications. Throughout the years, the gate has undergone several renovations and restorations, but its original architectural style has been remarkably preserved, serving as a testament to the city's storied past. The gate's unique blend of traditional Chinese and Western influences makes it a true architectural marvel that is sure to leave visitors in awe.

Today, Taipei North Gate is one of Taipei's most popular tourist attractions, and a true point of pride for the local community. The gate serves as a must-visit destination for anyone looking to explore Taipei's rich history and cultural heritage. A visit to this magnificent gate is an experience that cannot be missed, as it transports visitors back in time to a period of intense cultural exchange and creativity. In short, Taipei North Gate is a shining example of the importance of preserving our cultural heritage, and a testament to the creativity and ingenuity of the human spirit.

The park was originally established in 1900 as Taihoku New Park (臺北新公園; Pe̍h-ōe-jī: Tâi-oân Sin-kong-hn̂g) during the Japanese colonial period, on former temple grounds. It was the first European-style urban park in Taiwan, placed on the grounds of the Governor-General's Office.
In 1930, Taiwan's Japanese authorities established a radio station at the site designed by Kuriyama Shunichi (栗山俊一). The station initially housed the Taihoku Broadcasting Bureau, an arm of the Government-General Propaganda Bureau's Information Office. The following year, the Taiwan Broadcast Association was formed to handle island-wide broadcasts. The Taihoku Park radio station became the center of broadcast activity for the Association.
In 1935, it was one of the sites used for The Taiwan Exposition: In Commemoration of the First Forty Years of Colonial Rule.
After the handover of Taiwan from Japan to the Republic of China in 1945, the park was subsequently renamed Taipei New Park by the government.[citation needed] They renamed the broadcasting agency the Taiwan Broadcasting Company. The station became the primary broadcast organ of the Kuomintang government and military.

reviews.text:
The Taipei Rose Garden stands as a testament to the intricate interplay between nature and humanity, offering not just a respite from the urban chaos but also a canvas for contemplation on life's transient beauty and the enduring power of nature.

In its lush expanse, one finds a microcosm of existence, where the delicate petals of roses unfurl in a dance of ephemeral splendor. Here, amidst the fragrant whispers of blooming roses, one cannot help but reflect on the fleeting nature of life itself. Each bloom, radiant and captivating, serves as a poignant reminder of the cyclical rhythm of existence – from bud to blossom to eventual decay.

Yet, amidst this transience, there lies an undeniable sense of continuity and resilience. The roses, with their thorns and fragility, endure the passage of time, echoing the resilience of the human spirit in the face of life's inevitable challenges and adversities.

Moreover, the garden serves as a testament to the symbiotic relationship between humanity and nature. As visitors meander through its pathways, they are reminded of their interconnectedness with the natural world and the profound impact of their actions on the environment. In nurturing the roses, we nurture our own souls, fostering a deeper appreciation for the beauty and fragility of life.

In essence, the Taipei Rose Garden is more than just a horticultural marvel – it is a sanctuary for the soul, a place where one can pause, reflect, and find solace in the midst of life's complexities. It reminds us to cherish the fleeting moments of beauty, to embrace the impermanence of existence, and to find solace in the enduring power of nature's grace.

There are very beautiful wooden buildings here. It is the largest and most complete Japanese-style dormitory group in Taipei City. It is really rare to have such well-preserved monuments in the city center. It is worth visiting!
During the Qing Dynasty, Qidong Old Street was mostly used to transport coal, rice, grain and other livelihood necessities. In the Japanese period, the Japanese-style residential area of ​​Qidong Street was called the Xingmachi Official Housing Group. It was built from the 1920s to the 1940s. After the war, The Nationalist Government continued to use this area as a dormitory complex for central government officials. In 2006, this place was finally designated as a cultural asset. In 2009, the Ministry of Culture renovated this place and named this important building "Qidong Poetry Society". It is operated by the Taiwan Literature Museum and transformed into "Qidong Poetry Society" in 2020. Taiwan Literature Base".
There are 7 historical buildings in the Taiwan Literature Base. It is highly recommended to visit Qidong House first to understand the history of this area, and then look at other buildings. Matcha One’s matcha cake is also delicious, and it’s unique to dine in a Japanese-style building!
The Taiwan Literature Base is composed of 7 renovated Japanese-style buildings, including Qidong House, Yuedu Hall (the entrance is in the service center), Muse Garden, Creation Workshop, Exhibition Hall, Literature House and Heianjing (where the matcha shop Matcha One is located), 7 buildings Each has different themes and functions, which are quite rich!
The interior and exterior of the buildings in this area are very easy to photograph! The buildings and gardens are in very good condition, and the layout is thoughtful. The tatami mats are full of Japanese style, and it feels like walking into a time tunnel. The old Japanese dormitories, gravel paths, and sunlight filtering through the leaves between the buildings are full of poetry and history. Vicissitudes of life.

reviews.text:
Beautiful shrine! I’m glad I visited this place. I walked all the way from the Taipei Fine Arts Museum, in case you like to walk. There’s no fee to get inside. It’s very clean and well maintained. Lots of information if you’re a history buff.
Must-visit if you’re in Taipei.

We enjoyed our visit to the National Revolutionary Martyrs' Shrine while visiting Taipei. The shrine is beautiful. There is also information posted in English along the walls of the building, so we were able to better understand what we were seeing. The changing of the guards ceremony was nice to observe. It's free to enter, so no need to buy tickets unless you prefer to go with a tour group. Also, the bathrooms here are nice, clean, and spacious (in case nature calls).

Come see the ch singing of the guard which happens every hour. Stand on the side where the guards come out from the room (not the bathroom side). Then follow the guards to the building before they return to the front again. When they reach the front, I recommend standing outside to watch the guards change so you can see the twirling of the guns and changing of the guards at the post. It’s a more interesting show when viewed from there because if you’re inside you see the back view

This is a great place to learn more about the history of Taiwan. You will see depictions of key moments in their history that explains the events of what happened during the revolution of their people.

The National Revolutionary Martyrs Shrine is dedicated to the war dead of the Republic of China. It is set amidst quiet landscaped surroundings with a hourly changing of the guard. The inner sanctuary is guarded by two honour guards - a ceremonial drill display takes place here and along the route to the main entrance when the relief guards arrive.

There are toilets and a visitor lounge (beside the main entrance) - the latter has a free water dispenser and a vending machine where you can get a cold beverage from NTD 13 and up.

Definitely worth a visit - nearest MRT station is Dazhi Station where you can take a connecting bus to get to the shrine.

Graffiti Street in Taipei is an absolute treasure trove for street art enthusiasts. Visiting in February provided a unique glimpse into the vibrant art scene amidst a cooler climate. The narrow alleyways adorned with colorful murals and graffiti pieces were an explosion of creativity. Each corner unfolded a new story, a burst of colors, and diverse artistic styles, showcasing the talent and imagination of the local and international artists who've left their mark here.

The atmosphere was bustling yet laid-back, allowing ample time to appreciate the intricate details of the artwork while immersing oneself in the artistic energy of the place. What struck me most was the way the art seemed to interact with the surroundings, breathing life into the streets and creating an immersive experience for visitors.

Despite the bustling crowds, there was a sense of tranquility in discovering hidden gems and lesser-known artworks tucked away in unexpected corners. Whether a seasoned art enthusiast or a casual observer, Graffiti Street is a must-visit in Taipei, offering a dynamic canvas of urban artistry that evolves with each visit.

reviews.text: Free to visit but likely week day is best with lesser local crowds and international visitors. It is a steep climb for the physical fit or those whom "can" tolerate such a hike up to the small mount of 184 meters above the sea level. People with cardiovascular and/or respiratory conditions should reconsider this hike. However; there's AED equipment seen on the top of the mount rest area. Weak, elders, and children will have sections of few seats available "in sections" along the hike. Steep, small, and clean nature hike route paved with cobble stones, one way to go up and one way to get down. Be very careful with "all ages". Especially with the small children, do not run, and parents please hold their hands. This is a hiking route with "NO" safety guard rail. I've seen parents frustrated and struggled during the hike. Once you get on the mount top, it's amazing full view to see the entire Taipei skyline, especially on a good sunny day. Bring mosquito repellent, you'll needed it. No trash can seen on this hike, bring your own trash back to hotel.

If you’re taking a trip up to the top of Elephant mountain on a hot day, wear shorts and a tee. Not too difficult to hike up the steps with the occasional view of the city and mountains. On reaching the top expect an amazing view of Taipei including Taipei 101. When you get back down treat yourself to a well deserved Iced coffee from % ARABICA which has the coolest AC ever.

A quick 20-30 minutes hike near Taipei City which offers a great view of the Taipei 101. The path is well lit and has steps all along the way, you can find people here all the time and a lot of people visit during late evening for the view.
Elevation might be difficult for people who are new to hikes, take breaks and you can make it to the peak easily.
Exactly as promised on the postcards. Choice of viewing platforms when you are at the top. Steps once exiting the park are quite steep, so take your time.

Beautiful panoramic views all the way up the climb. It's around 20 minutes of just stairs which can be quite intense but I promise the views, day or night, are worth it and incredible. There weren't too many people when I went so it was relatively easy to get good photos. There are at least four different good photo spots all with Taipei 101 in the background so you've got plenty of choice!

reviews.text:
The “Moon Bus,” located near Taipei 101, is a captivating tourist attraction inspired by a beloved Taiwanese picture book. This whimsical installation transports visitors into a fantastical world that feels straight out of a storybook. As you step inside the bus, you’re enveloped in a dreamlike atmosphere that sparks the imagination.

The interior design is enchanting, with colorful decorations and creative elements that reflect the themes of the original picture book. One of the highlights is the reflective mirror at the end of the bus, which creates an ethereal effect and adds to the overall enchanting experience. The mirror gives visitors the impression of stepping into another dimension, enhancing the magical feel of the attraction.

Visiting the Moon Bus is a delightful experience for both children and adults, making it a perfect stop if you’re exploring the area around Taipei 101.

I passed this bus while I was walking around Taipei. The bus itself looks very cute. It’s seems the bus is inspired by a Taiwanese children book (I haven’t read it). You can enter the bus, and it’s gives you a very dreamy feeling.

The color selection and design are gorgeous. I can’t imagine how much time the artist spent working on this exhibit. I want to take this exhibit home with me! 🌙 🌕 🌖 ✨ 🙌🙏
Finally got the time to visit this bus at the end of my day in Taiwan. Super cool, especially the inner end of the bus! 🌝

Emooly's passion for Taipei's Golden Age shines brilliantly throughout her walking tour. Her encyclopedic knowledge of North Gate's dramatic preservation, the historic Railway Ministry Park, and Dihua Street's evolution from merchant hub to creative district is delivered with infectious enthusiasm. What sets Emooly apart is her exceptional curiosity - she doesn't just recite facts about Fa Zhu Gong Temple or Xia-Hai City God Temple, but weaves compelling narratives that bring Dadaocheng's 1920s literary scene to life. Her insightful commentary on how traditions blend with innovations reflects her own promising future. With her intellectual curiosity and storytelling gifts, Emooly's path forward appears limitless. I enjoyed the Formosa free walking tour on 8 March afternoon. Thanks Formosa tours, bringing the memories again into light.

Anil Dhope, India

Entertaining to do but food choices don’t look very appealing if you’re used to food in the west. Beef pepper buns are probably the best this night market has to offer. Rest of the food did not look appealing or you get deep fried everything. And the claw machines are all scams - the operators place other stuffed animals in a way that will limit any toy from falling into the bin - pay close attention and you’ll notice it too. It’s sad cause it’s all the kids who are trying to win a toy and just end up frustrated from losing all their money. The claw machines in Japan don’t cheat you like they do in this market. And for restrooms, good luck finding one. We asked a food vendor for the closest restroom, and she pointed us to a temple nearby. If you’re short on time and hungry, this night market can be skipped. Taipei has so many good restaurants, that risking your dinner to the night market choices is a foolish move. Don’t recommend this place at all unless you just wanna check it off your list to say you’ve been there. Won’t ever come back, and honestly, might skip the other night markets in Taipei as well.

A mountain friend once said that he had been to all the peaks of Si Beast Mountain, but could not find Shishan Peak.
Indeed, the trailhead is not easy to find. As long as you go west from the right side of Songshan Road, the industrial road in front of Lingyin Temple, you will see a small sign, and you are right to go up.
There are primitive trails along the way, and the hillside is not steep. It is very easy to walk and can be reached in about 10 minutes.
Three years ago, there was no sign. Today, because I had to guide mountain friends from Taichung, I accompanied them up. I was surprised to find that there was a wooden monument to the Lion Peak. When I took the photo, I could still see 101 in the distance. I was very happy😃!
In the past, if you walked straight down the mountain, there would be a small steep slope that required pulling a rope. Today, it seems to be overgrown with weeds, so you can only turn back the same way.
Come and explore if you have the chance!

Nestled in the heart of Taichung, just a short walk from the famous Miyahara dessert shop, the Green River Waterfront Landscape Trail offers a refreshing escape from the city’s hustle. This beautifully designed riverside walkway combines lush greenery, modern urban aesthetics, and historical charm, making it a perfect spot for a leisurely stroll, a morning jog, or a relaxing break after indulging in Miyahara’s famous ice cream.

The trail follows the Green River, with well-maintained paths lined with trees, flowers, and stylish seating areas. At night, the area comes alive with subtle lighting that highlights the water and bridges, creating a romantic ambiance. Thoughtfully placed art installations and historical markers add cultural depth, making it more than just a scenic walk—it’s an experience that connects nature with Taichung’s evolving cityscape.

A nice, family-friendly place for a stroll! There are mini waterfalls, a small stone bridge, and koi swimming along the way. Retaining walls provide seating, and stairs connect to bridges and roadways. Lots of nearby dessert shops and stores to visit as you walk.

The lights at night were spectacular! This place is an oasis in the middle of suburban Taichung. The water is clear and the koi swimming around seem happy too. I spotted some ducks swimming too. The landscape was well designed and the greens and trees brought fresh air. There were however a number of mendicants and homeless people especially beneath the bridge.

Visiting Rainbow Village in Taichung after the passing of its creator, Rainbow Grandpa, is a bittersweet experience. While the vibrant colors and cheerful murals remain intact, there’s an undeniable sense of nostalgia and reverence for the man who brought this small village to life.
Rainbow Grandpa’s story continues to resonate deeply with visitors. His dedication to transforming a forgotten military village into a lively and meaningful space is a testament to the power of art and passion. Even in his absence, his spirit lives on through every stroke of paint that adorns the walls.
The local community and organizations have stepped up to preserve Rainbow Village, ensuring that his legacy endures. The murals are maintained regularly, and there are ongoing efforts to promote the site as a cultural and historical landmark. Visiting now feels like paying homage to a visionary whose work inspired countless people.
While you can no longer meet Rainbow Grandpa in person, the village offers a tranquil atmosphere to reflect on the stories he left behind. Informational signs and videos onsite share his journey, making it easy for new visitors to understand the significance of his work.
Overall, Rainbow Village remains a must-visit destination. It’s more than just a collection of colorful murals—it’s a celebration of one man’s love for art and his determination to create joy. Rainbow Grandpa may be gone, but his dream continues to inspire and uplift all who visit.

I think it’s still worth a trip out to visit, but I wish the gift shop was still in function! The old gift shop was fantastic. And that they had pictures of the original artwork by the new paintings—so you could see what it used to look like.

Taitang Lakeside Ecological Trail is located in the East District of Taichung City. It surrounds Xingquan Lake (Taitang Lakeside Ecological Park) with a total length of about 2 kilometers. It takes about 20 minutes to walk around the lake. You can also ride a bicycle around the lake. Willow trees and other plants are planted around the trail, creating a cool environment. There are multiple viewing platforms along the way, providing an excellent perspective on the lake scenery.

The floor tiles on the trail are also decorated with leaf rubbings, adding to the ingenuity. The park also retains the Taichung Sales Office of the Imperial Sugar Refinery during the Japanese colonial period, which has been revitalized into an exhibition space. It also has restaurants and cafes, such as Ye Tang and 1935 Cafe & Bar, for visitors to relax and dine.

In addition, the Yongquan Park Civilization Base around the trail is open to climb the tower during the day, overlooking the panoramic view of the Imperial Sugar Factory and Lakeside Park, making it a good place to take photos. The entire park combines natural landscape with history and culture, becoming an oasis of beauty in downtown Taichung.

The leisurely lake-circling trail next to Taichung Station is full of flowing willow branches along the lake. It is particularly leisurely and leisurely to walk on. It is recommended that foreign tourists take a walk around it while waiting for the bus.

Amazing building that has tonnes of space inside   It. Amazing large window view scape of all the high rise buildings in the near by housing areas.  Built in segments and slotted together like a ship.

There's a huge outside area of the theatre with a fountain [but didn't work when I came here]. There's a mini river with water that flows inside the theatre, which I think is really cool! There's gift shops, eating places, some museums here, as well as theatres where some shows would have their venues here! There's lifts here too, and there's a rooftop area at the 6th floor [also the highest floor of this theatre]. The views are fire though! You can see high rise buildings and roads from all 4 sides of the theatre, and if you're lucky, catch the sunset here! There's a small cafe at the 5th floor, and overall, you should definitely visit this place, since it's free!

reviews.text: Paid 1280 NTD for 3 people for the Garden + BBQ package. Went on a Sunday so there was a crowd, but we went in early so we were able to get a lot of photos first. The garden is not that big as the internet suggests, but still aesthetically pleasing. The bbq is so-so. It’s quite far from the train station so it’s much better to arrange for a service beforehand to avoid getting scammed by the taxis there.

A lovely place with a decent-sized garden featuring a wide variety of flowers. The views are beautiful, and it’s a great spot for photos. You can also find small strawberries to enjoy. A nice place to visit if you love flowers and nature!

The flower garden is a stunning and well-maintained place filled with vibrant colors and fresh fragrances. The variety of flowers creates a breathtaking view. The pathways are clean, and the atmosphere is peaceful, making it a perfect spot for relaxation or photography. The garden’s layout is thoughtfully designed, allowing visitors to explore different floral arrangements with ease. Beautiful garden ornaments are scattered throughout, adding charm to the scenery.

We took the train to get there, and a 20-minute walk from the station. For a more convenient trip, I recommend taking a taxi or renting a bike. Another option for commuters is to take the Fengyuan bus, which provides easier access to the garden. For those driving, there is a large parking area available, and parking is free.

The garden also offers plenty of seating, with benches and tables placed throughout for visitors to rest and enjoy the surroundings. There is a food area where you can grab a meal, as well as vending machines for quick snacks and drinks. Entry to the general garden area is free, but there is a fee to access the designated flower fields zone. If you're looking for a place to go to or looking for a peaceful escape, this garden is a great place to visit.

Random but they have a huge buffet BBQ where you grab the food yourself from the fridge and grill it. If you order the BBQ the flower market entry is complimentary, but we came with a group so we didn’t try it.

The entrance fee is about 150 NT. Lots of beautiful flowers in a variety of colors to admire and photograph. IG girlies will love this place, they have different flowers reflecting the different seasons.

Zhongshe Flower Market in Taichung is an enchanting and picturesque destination that's a true paradise for flower enthusiasts and photographers alike. This expansive garden is a riot of colors, with beautifully landscaped fields of vibrant flowers stretching as far as the eye can see. From tulips and roses to sunflowers and lavender, each season brings a new wave of blooming beauty, making it a delightful place to visit year-round.

One of the standout features of Zhongshe Flower Market is its variety of themed gardens and Instagram-worthy spots. Whether you're strolling through the romantic rose garden or posing by the iconic flower archways, there's no shortage of stunning backdrops for your photos. The market also offers unique experiences like picking your own flowers and creating custom bouquets, adding an interactive element to your visit.

The facilities at Zhongshe Flower Market are well-maintained, with convenient amenities like on-site cafes and picnic areas, allowing you to relax and enjoy the serene environment. The market is also family-friendly, with plenty of space for children to run around and explore.

Overall, Zhongshe Flower Market is a must-visit for anyone in Taichung. Its breathtaking floral displays, charming atmosphere, and ample photo opportunities make it a perfect spot for a day of leisure and beauty. Whether you're a nature lover or simply looking for a picturesque escape, Zhongshe Flower Market is sure to impress and leave you with lasting memories. 🌸📸

I hope you enjoy your visit to this floral wonderland! 🌺🌷

There are three bathrooms I'm familiar with, the first and southern most is located on level B1 of the tall commercial building on the NE corner of Yucai S Street. This is also the main intersection for the food vendors.

The second is at the Family Mart along the middle, opposite the school and the third is on level B1 of the outdoor mall that anchors the northern end.

To be honest, the No.1 Middle School Night Market seems a bit less bustling compared to Fengjia Night Market. However, it's still worth a visit. I took photos of all the delicious food and interesting things I found there.

It’s a fun night market geared to students and less for children. Lots of food stalls but less variety than Fong Jia night market. They have good stinky tofu and lots of fried foods available. The shopping here is good too with lots of clothes and jewelry and random stores. There aren’t very much garbage cans so you have to carry your garbage until you find one. You can find some very affordable food here like 4 dumplings for 20 NT.

Less vendors than I remember.....

I went to a vocational college here for 3 years and gee... that was a LOT of vendors then. But my hubby enjoyed the fried chicken steak very much still.

A great alternative to Fengjia Night Market, Yizhong Night Market was more accessible from our hotel, so we decided to visit it instead—and we weren’t disappointed. The market offered a wide variety of delicious food choices, and the atmosphere was lively. It turned out to be a perfect spot for a late-night snack, and we really enjoyed exploring the local flavors. Definitely worth a visit!

The DIY Sun Cake Workshop is a must-try if you visit Taichung! The instructor was friendly and very knowledgeable on the history and process of making Sun Cakes. Each person will get to make 6 Sun Cakes and it comes it a cute box!

You can sign up through their website but it is in Chinese, so you will need to translate. There is a maximum as well as minimum pax for each lesson, so book early (1-2 weeks before) but be prepared for timeslot changes if your selected timeslot has too few participants. The lesson itself is also in Chinese so it would be useful to have someone who understands Chinese join in... otherwise you can just follow the motion... haha

The museum itself is just some panels of information so it's not that interesting. The highlight is really the DIY workshop.

We signed up for a DIY sun cake class at the museum. The instructor had decades of sun cake baking experience. Very patient and interactive. He was passionate about his craft and an ambassador of promoting this treasured Taichung delicacy. The sun cake was DELICIOUS 😋  Communication with the staff was top-notched. Everyone was welcoming and made our visit to the museum the most enjoyable. Upstairs is the museum that not only explains the history of sun cake, but also the architecture of the building and the surrounding neighborhood. Also have an art show of drawings and paintings.
We highly recommend this museum and especially the DIY class. One of the most fun things we've done in Taichung so far.

reviews.text: Very beautiful Confucius temple in Taichung. Peaceful, great to take a look in deep details of Chinese architecture and perfect for taking photos

This temple is a hidden gem in Taichung City, especially if you love traditional Chinese architecture. We loved the quiet and calm atmosphere, making it the best place for a retreat or a break from the busy city life. Some people were taking pictures, while others were just sitting and enjoying the moment.

The Confucius Temple in Taichung is a serene and culturally rich destination that offers a deep dive into traditional Chinese architecture and philosophy. The temple grounds are beautifully maintained, providing a peaceful escape from the city’s hustle and bustle. The architecture is stunning, with intricate carvings, grand halls, and serene courtyards that reflect the principles of Confucianism. Informative plaques and exhibits provide valuable insights into Confucius’s teachings and their historical significance. Whether you’re interested in history, culture, or simply looking for a tranquil spot to relax, the Confucius Temple is a must-visit. Highly recommended for its beauty, tranquility, and educational value!

Japanese style, small place, have coffee shop, I feel peaceful when I came here

This is the old Japanese style buildings area from back when the Japanese occupied Taiwan.   Now, the buildings have been refurbished as a museum for tourists.   The general area is beautiful with big trees and some very knowledgeable guides to explain the buildings and their functions.   Nice experience.

The Taichung Literature Museum is another hidden gem in Taichung. Originally constructed as a police dormitory in 1934 during the Japanese era, these buildings were designated as historical buildings by the Cultural Affairs Bureau of Taichung City Government in 2009. In April 2010, the city government renovated the buildings and transformed them into the Taichung Literature Museum to honor literary contributions and promote literature in Taiwan.

Best public space we've visited in taichung. Great crowd, unique stalls, and plenty of cozy seating corners to lounge as you bask under the sun and enjoy the chill vibes.

Free access for all.

reviews.text: A very majestic bronze statue, which brings back a lot of memories and is a great check-in point.
A cool status of the Lich King Arthas.  Recommend you come when there is good natural lighting because the lighting here isn't too good.  The statue is huge.
For all fans of Warcraft. Amazing statue 👌
I think this is the best spot for sunset. I have never seen such beautiful sight

This statue is located within a park in Taichung City, and it provides a remarkable portrayal of one of my favorite video game characters, Arthas Menethil from "Warcraft." The staute expertly captures his most iconic appearance, featuring his medieval-style armor. However, what left the most impression on me is the inclusion of the "Lich King's helmet,"and in his right hand, he holds the evil sword, "Frostmourne."These two items symbolize him who was turned into a powerful enemy from a admired prince by dark forces.

The lifelike 1:1 scale of the statue made it feel as if Arthas  were standing right in front of me, leaving me shocked very much. By the way, during my visit, I noticed that one of the bone spurs on his left shoulder plate had unexpectedly broken. This accident made me reflect on the statue's maintenance,and also reminded us to pay more attention to these artworks.

Dome of Light feature is located right after you tap out of the formasa train station gantry.

This huge and beautifully created feature is made up of pieces and pieces of stain glasses and I feel its definitely worth to spend some time and appreciate when passing by.

However, the "show" is kind of disappointing as it seems more like an advert projected on the floor.

Beautiful stained glass roof and occasional light shows with music. Show times are written on the board by the dome.
It’s a pretty place to pass by on the way to the night markets.

A must-stop-by if you visit Kaohsiung! The tourist crowd wasn't very big in weekdays, and we were able to take photos of the whole circular area without too much interferences and photobombs from fellow travellers.

this place is located in the station itself, and does not need much time. At night around 8 or 9, light shows with music are organized which is pretty good.

Was told by the local this is probably the most beautiful MRT station in Taiwan. A small pet store is located inside the park. Numbers of artist performing in the park. Best place for family time with children.

So beautiful at night! Can be crowded especially as you exit the train station but definitely still walkable and passable. A lot happening with crowds of youngsters, tourists, families. Marvelous light display for the holidays !

I can say that the attractions in Taiwan are very beautiful. 🇹🇼

Nice pond with different temples that can be visited. Lots of turtles can be seen in certain areas, while some elderly enjoy themselves in a nice karaoke session.

Overall, a nice atmosphere.

reviews.text: We enjoyed this so much compared to Shilin in Taipei. There plenty of seats and it’s spacious. We liked everything we got - cheese coin, taiwanese fried chix, dumplings, and bubble tea.

Liuhe Night Market is a must visit spot in Kaohsiung, especially if you’re staying nearby. It’s conveniently located less than 2 km from major hotels like the Intercontinental, making it an easy walk or a quick Uber ride for under $5.

The market comes alive in the evening, with vibrant stalls lining the street, offering a fantastic variety of local street food, from iconic seafood dishes to bubble tea and grilled delicacies. The atmosphere is buzzing with energy, and the friendly vendors add to the charm of the place.

Whether you’re craving fresh seafood, want to try Taiwan’s famous papaya milk, or just want to soak in the lively night market vibe, Liuhe delivers. It’s a perfect spot to experience local flavors and culture, all within easy reach of your hotel.

An enjoyable night market to grab different kinds of street food. Prices similar to Thailand,  have public toilets across the road. Visit this market it's recommended to have seafood cause the place is near the harbour. I found the Taiwan custard apples are very nice sweet and juicy. Recommended to try

I went here for 2 consecutive nights and it was raining so I'm not sure if that's the reason why there's only few opened stalls. But compared to the other night markets I've been to in Kaohsiung, this is the most organized and caters more to tourists.

reviews.text: It's truly wonderful to come here at night, feel the sea breeze, and chat with friends or ride bikes nearby. However, we should be cautious about traffic safety as there are many cars on the narrow roads. There are also many delicious food options nearby, but parking can be a bit inconvenient.

This is a place that is near and dear to my heart. Lots of memories here. Located right next to Shoushan (where the macaque monkeys are) and Sun Yat Sen University. It might be a little bit tricky to get there because its technically “one street in” but shouldn’t be hard with google maps.

They must’ve remodeled the place in the past 10-15 years..who knows, but there is now a clearly marked paid parking lot, clean landscaping for people to walk and enjoy the sea view/sunset, bathrooms, and a few vendors/shops selling food. Behind the bathrooms you’ll also find some stairs that lead to higher vantage points and even some old cannons and forts.

In the same area, right next to the entrance of the university is a steep road that goes up the hill to a temple (十八王公廟). The old superstition is that couples will end up splitting if they visit the place. You can climb the stairs or somehow get up the hill~don’t even attempt unless you have a really strong scooter. Trust me lol.

Not sure if they allow people to go into the university grounds anymore, but if they allow, theres a breakwater area right after you enter that is great during sunsets and can be a quiet, romantic place at night. Also some peaceful and quiet beaches deeper inside—do be careful because waves can be rough. Theres really not a whole lot to do, but great for couples and families to get some fresh air from the Kaohsiung port. If you’re all the way here, make sure you ride the boat to Cijin nearby and visit Pier 2 and KW2 the port warehouse.

The scenic area is situated near Nation Sat Yen Sen university and it is well connected to public transportation. The Scenic area is a combination of many walking and driving trails near the sea shores with some good food carts and a cafeteria, especially in the evening time. The place is clean and well maintained but sometimes needs to be attentive to streets animals.

Located on the west side of Kaohsiung City, at the foothills of the southwestern tip of Shoushan, Xiziwan is bordered by Wanshou Mountain in the north, and the Cijin Peninsula in the south. It is about 20 minutes drive from the city center. It is surrounded by mountains and the sea, and the scenery is pleasant. When the night falls, the sea is magnificent and the fishing boats are shining. The sunset at Xiziwan is one of the eight scenic spots in Kaohsiung, and the beauty of the sea and sky is beautiful. At dusk, it is often seen that couples of lovers are in love with each other, and the situation is more poetic and picturesque. (Photo taken by pixel 3a)

There’s not a lot of serene places in the city, so this one’s already good if you just want to look at the sea, enjoy the sun, and just be out of the busy city without going too far. You can see the lighthouse of Cijin/Qijin Island from this area (see my uploaded photo) and there are also nice “shaved ice” shops around it if you want something cold in the summer. It’s better to go there at daytime because night can be very dark. Nighttime is only good if the sky is clear and you just want to see the stars. Took off stars because I didn’t see any shaded seats when we went there so it was very hot when it’s sunny. The seatings were all under the sun. Meaning, you won’t consider staying here. Might as well just take photos then leave.

reviews.text: Singuang Riverside Park is a serene oasis amidst the bustling city skyscrapers. Whether spending quality time with loved ones, walking your pet, or taking a bicycle ride, it's a must-stop. Best of all, there's a free water park that's perfect for some fun time with the children. Highly recommended!

This park is a wonderful place for walking especially in the morning for local residents; and, maybe in the evening for sightseeing visitors. It locates at middle of Kaohsiung port surrounded by travelers center (in construction), world trade and exhibition center, 85 sky tower and city library.

One of the best places to visit and just relax, whenever I stop by the park I always spend hours relaxing and talking with friends and family. The best time to come is during the night where it is cool and comfortable. During this time we can enjoy the scenery and harbor. The harbor at night is really nice and calming. There is always some boats parked on the side. That gives it a very ecstatic look and makes it feel like a harbor. But with the park like side that have a lot of seats and places to look. The area has also some photo worthy shots of sculptures and a walk through walkway that goes up and gives you a better view of the whole harbor and water side. The place also is big enough for a lot of people. So if it's a weekend there is still a lot of space in the park to give you privacy. The park also include a small bar on the side of the harbor that you can reserve or walk in to have a nice sun set drink. The place can be a little expensive and there might be a lot of people. Depending on the day or holiday. But if you are lucky enough you can have the whole place to yourself. As this place can be quite expensive but is worth it if you ask me. The night may be my preferred time to visit. But the day visit is also very good and I've come here a few times during the day and it was worth while. I brought some food and had a nice picnic on one of the benches. If you are lucky you could see some activities that people sometimes do in the park. From Exhibition beside the park to locals bringing their parrots to the park to fly around. These are some of those things that not a lot of people post but if you have been here for a while you can see them. Hope this can help people know sometimes the simple places can be the most memorable ones.

A nice park with beautiful pier view and different style yachts. A restaurant next to the pier provides outdoor seats for custumers to enjoy view on the bank. After dark, an indoor pub, next to the pier as well, can accompany to you for the rest of night.

The yacht is for rent too. We were cruising around Kaushiung harbor and enjoied an excellent gourmate meal to spend a terrific evening.
Offers a great view of the 85 Tower and the port. Many families with their children and dogs here, as well as young couples on a date.

Nice spot to come here and relax; free entrance.
Wide green park available, you can see locals come here for a walk, petting, picnic, or some other family events.
Old rail section is preserved and you can walk on the old rail track on bridge, and see the real trains passing by.
Great photo spot.
Historical brick kiln house is also just nearby, and you can experience some old time farm building and history.  Taiwan local souvenirs are also available here.

A very memorable railroad that I have had traveled on for many years. It used to be a single railway shared by both directions. It took around 3 quarters to an hour to travel between Kaohsiung and Pingtung when the train was powered by diesel engine. Time consuming, but somehow fun when looking back now.

reviews.text: If this is your first time visiting Kaohsiung, start here. It is only open from November to April, and you must be accompanied by a professional mountain guide. You can use the Chaisan website, but since I am a foreigner, I made a reservation using a company called kkday. The guide is very enthusiastic and takes me to hidden caves and secret places. Also be lucky enough to meet gentle wild monkeys. Of course, you must leave the monkey alone and do not feed it.
Amazing cave
good

It takes some physical strength to climb halfway up the mountain
Then bring a headlamp and helmet⛑️ to explore the cave
The part with the small climbing rope
Open from November to April every year
✅You need to apply to enter, otherwise you will be fined 3,000
✅Need to be led by a qualified childcare team leader
✅There must be strong sunshine at 12 noon

Currently, it is closed from May to October during the restricted period because the ground is very slippery during the rainy season and is really dangerous.
It will open in November. Application is required. Professional tour guides will take you in. You can visit more secret places and it is safer. We will also help participants prepare helmets (there is a penalty of 3,000 yuan for not bringing them) and headlamps. Unfortunately, it is too early to enter. No light can shine into the cave. This time we only saw one monkey waiting on the tree for us to come out of the cave. This registration information is for registration within the senior class of Line 104.

reviews.text: Chilling vibe. Good spot for activities or exhibitions. This region is getting better and prosperous.

✍️I found that the night view on Pier 2 is so fresh and free from any interference. My favorite attractions are performances, special activities, food, exhibitions, and creative paintings. Beautiful scenery and good places include: Maolin Mountain Tour, Meinong Hakka Old Street for food, Qishan Old Street for food and shopping, Jiaxian Old Street for taro ice shopping, Cijin Old Street for seafood, Yancheng District Old Street New Year Market, the most famous Ganggoat Meat Dishes, and Hongmaogang Garden. Places to go to watch boats and participate in activities, Weiwuying Dadong Cultural Center ⭐Pier 2⭐The night view is beautiful. I have been to the Manchu Cultural Festival in Northeast China, Mongolian activities in Inner Mongolia, and Kazakhstan in my life. My favorite thing in my life is traveling around the mountains and rivers. I will retire as soon as possible and live the life I want, such as traveling around the island, studying at the university, taking the civil service exam and getting the financial product certificate with continued success, eating delicious meals, and living in the mountains in peace and quiet. 💯
The Pier-2 Art Zone runs parallel to the light rail track, and this road has a homonym of "asphalt road". Great place for walking.

Piyou Road is a very interesting road name
The name symbolizes the path that must be taken during recreation in Pier 2 Art Zone.
Pieryou Road itself also runs through almost all attractions in the Pier-2 Art Zone.
Jufanhama Star Train, Dayi Warehouse Area, Pier 2 Station, Robot Toilet
Even all the way to the revolving bridge at the end and the Kaohsiung Pop Music Center are within the scope of the barge tour.
There are also Kaohsiung light rail lines along the way.
Hama Star, Pier 2 Penglai, Pier 2 Dayi
All the way to True Love Pier Station
The whole walk actually took one morning.
———
Most of the scenic spots along the way are outdoors.
So be sure to bring water with you when you go out
Otherwise, it’s easy to get heatstroke while shopping
———
Recently there is a special exhibition with the creator nearby
If you are interested, you can stop by and have a look nearby.

You walk up a short hill to the fort and then there are lots of fun stairs to climb. Great view of the city scape and my favorite spot on Cijin. Free entry as well, like all the tourist spots here.

Cihou Fort is a historic fort in the Cijin District of Kaohsiung, Taiwan, which formerly guarded the northern entrance to Kaohsiung Harbor.

From the fort, you can enjoy a beautiful view of the South China Sea as well as the Kaohsiung cityscape on the other side.

I loved wandering around here, on a weekday morning I was the only one there. There are some great views of the city and water, and the fort itself is in good condition, with stairs to get up to the top of it.

Kaohsiung's tram is my favorite. It connects many tourist attractions to a loop, making them easily accessible to visitors. With a little walking or biking, you can get to most of the tourist spots in this city.
This green tunnel feels to me like a surprising gift. The trees and their shadows carry the tram, and the tram carries us, like we are tripping into Hayao Miyazaki's movie.
This way, the tram is not only a transport vehicle, but also a hideaway from the bully of the tropical sun. 🌞
You can’t really see the green tunnel while on the light rail, so do hop out at the nearest stop and you can see it!

A must if you’re in the area. Kaohsiung LRT’s green tunnel is a scenic ride through a lush, tree-lined passage that stretches from one station to another (about a city block). This is one of my favorite portions of the track where you can enjoy views of greenery from every angle of the train. Very photogenic spots - people get off at the station just to take a pictures of the trains coming and going thru the tunnel.

👣Travel by heart:
Kaohsiung Secret Sharing
watch the sunset
Chikan Beach/Ziguan/Zhixin Night Market

Today we came to a secret place called Chikan Beach.
At first I thought it was near the Chikan Tower in Tainan, but it turned out not to be.
This place is located near Oyster House.

Here we are,
I unexpectedly found a piece of cyanotype installation art.
I’ve seen it before in Tainan, and it instantly felt familiar and surprising!

Keep going forward,
The view is wide, facing the sea and the sunset.
Although there is no beach here, there are wave absorbing blocks in front.
But sitting by the embankment, enjoying the sea breeze, listening to the sound of the waves, and quietly watching the sunset, the tranquility is very relaxing.

At first I thought I wouldn’t see the sunset today.
Because the thick clouds blocked the sun later,
Unexpectedly, at the last moment, the sun penetrated the clouds and set. The changes in light and shadow in the sky were really beautiful.

After watching the sunset, I ran to the nearby Zhixin Night Market.
Feel free to wander around, eat and drink, and feel the lively atmosphere of the place.
The whole day ended like this, ordinary but full of beauty!
